title: Board/Kanban view must render grouped columns with drag-drop card reordering
intent: Kanban board is the primary visual workflow organizing tool; must support column grouping by state/priority/assignee, card drag-drop within/across columns, and WIP limits
acceptance: Columns render per group_by selection
Cards drag within column and to other columns
Column headers show group name and card count
Drop target indicators appear during drag
View switches to kanban without data loss
anti_patterns: No drop zone highlight during drag
WIP limit not displayed or uneditable
Drag only works for card text, not card area
interactions: edit WIP limit in column header
manual_simulation: Switch to board view grouped by state
incentive: Board is most common workflow UI; drag-drop affordance must be discoverable and responsive

title: Board columns must collapse/expand to hide and show grouped items
intent: Dense boards with many columns or items need column collapse for focus and horizontal scroll reduction
acceptance: Collapse icon appears in column header
Collapsed column shows only header and count
Expanded state restores full column view
Collapse state persists per board session or per saved view
anti_patterns: Collapse icon without visual indicator of collapsed state
No count visible on collapsed column
Collapse state not removable without UI reload
Collapsed columns cause horizontal shift/layout thrash
incentive: Column collapse is key to usable dense boards without side-scroll friction

title: Board columns must support editable WIP limits with warnings and visual indicators
intent: WIP limits prevent overload and encourage focusing on completing work; must be visually obvious without requiring config panels
acceptance: WIP limit editable inline in column header
Column header shows current/max counts
Color or warning when count >= limit
Limit persists to project settings or view
Can disable limit per column
anti_patterns: WIP limit only in settings panel, not visible in column
Negative or zero limits accepted without validation
incentive: WIP limits are core flow practice; visibility drives adoption

title: List view must render rows per item with inline edit and density controls
intent: List is dense, scannable alternative to board; must support multi-level grouping, inline editing, and visibility toggle for columns
acceptance: Items render as table rows with grouping headers
Group headers collapse/expand sub-items
Click cell to inline-edit field
Columns show/hide via menu
Row hover shows actions (open detail, etc)
anti_patterns: Column visibility toggle missing or hard to find
Mobile list is unreadable or clipped
interactions: swipe left on mobile for actions
critique_focus: inline edit UX and validation feedback
incentive: List view is power-user favorite; must not feel like reduced-feature fallback

title: Spreadsheet view must support column reorder, resize, show/hide with persistence
intent: Power users need column customization for task tracking; changes must persist to saved view or user preference
acceptance: Columns reorderable via drag in header
Column width resizable via edge drag
Column visibility toggle in menu
Changes persist to saved view config
Mobile: horizontal scroll with column indicator
anti_patterns: Column drag requires shift-click or hidden menu
Resize via drag has no cursor feedback
Hide column removes it from menu permanently without recovery
Spreadsheet requires horizontal scroll >20% of the time without indicator
incentive: Column customization is key to task-tracking adoption; persistence avoids setup friction

title: All views must support sorting by any displayed field with asc/desc toggle
intent: Sorting is fundamental to rapid task triage; must be accessible without menus and must show current sort order
acceptance: Click column header to sort ascending
Click again to sort descending
Visual indicator shows current sort field and direction
Sort options available for all sortable columns
Mobile: sort menu accessible without horizontal scroll
anti_patterns: Sort only available in advanced settings menu
No indicator of current sort direction
Sort by field not sortable (e.g. key)
Mobile sort menu clipped off screen
Clicking header toggles visibility instead of sort
critique_focus: sort options for special fields (key, estimate, etc)
manual_simulation: Check mobile sort menu position and visibility
incentive: Sort is most-used view control; header affordance drives discoverability

title: All views must support group-by dimension selection with sub-group option
intent: Grouping is the primary lens for workflow visibility; must be swappable without data loss and support multi-level grouping
acceptance: Group-by dropdown shows available dimensions (state, assignee, label, priority, cycle, module, target_date)
Selecting group-by re-groups items without data loss
Sub-group option available for 2-level grouping
Empty groups collapsible or hideable
Group-by persists to saved view
anti_patterns: Changing group-by loses filter or sort state
Sub-group not available when useful (e.g. state + assignee)
Empty groups take excessive vertical space
Group-by options not documented per view type
manual_simulation: Save as new view with both
incentive: Group-by is power tool for workflow lens changes; must be instant and reversible

title: Views must support rich filters: state, assignee, label, priority, due date, cycle, module, custom fields
intent: Filters narrow focus to relevant work; must be composable and saveable without menu fatigue
acceptance: Filter button opens persistent filter panel
Multiple filters combinable (AND logic)
Each filter type has appropriate UI (chips for labels, date picker for due date, etc)
Clear/reset filters button
Filtered view can be saved as named view with filters baked in
Filter state shows count badge
anti_patterns: Filter only available in rare advanced view
Filters in dropdown that closes after each selection
No AND/OR logic choice (locked to AND)
Filter UI doesn't match field type (dropdown for date)
Filters lost when switching views or after reload
critique_focus: mobile filter menu size and scrolling
manual_simulation: Load saved view and verify filters applied
incentive: Filters are the second-most-used control; UI must not punish composition

title: Single filter builder powers every work layout
intent: Replace ad hoc filters with one Plane-style filter builder for status/state group, assignee, label, cycle, module, type, priority, date, dependency, run state, doc link, and search filters.
acceptance: Filter builder renders the same model in board, list, spreadsheet, calendar, timeline, reports, CLI, and TUI.
Applied filters are visible as removable chips with counts where known.
Filter query serializes to URL and SavedView without lossy field conversion.
Unsupported filters on a surface are marked unavailable rather than silently dropped.
anti_patterns: Each layout implements its own filter semantics.
Stringly typed filters that cannot validate field names or operators.
Search box pretending to be full filter builder.
interactions: Add assignee plus no-due-date plus blocked-by filter and save it.
Remove one applied chip and confirm task counts update without losing sort.
Open same saved filter in CLI/TUI and compare result count.
critique_focus: Does the filter model map Plane work-item power filters to Fulcrum-specific run/doc/context fields cleanly?
manual_simulation: Find all tasks assigned to me that have failed agent runs and no linked doc, then save that view.
incentive: Prevents every new work surface from forking query behavior.

title: Watch Active ACP Session
intent: Humans observe real-time streamed messages, tool calls, file edits, approvals, and errors as agents execute
acceptance: Web: timeline shows transcript, tool calls with args/results, diff previews, pending approvals. CLI: `fulcrum runs watch <id> --json` streams events. No scrolling jumps; autoscroll toggle visible.
anti_patterns: Streamed content jumps without scroll lock
critique_focus: Do all tool calls show: name, args summary, result status, and copy button?
manual_simulation: Start a run, open Web live view, verify transcript streams in real-time, click tool calls to expand, check diff previews
incentive: Agents work in isolation; humans need live visibility to intervene.

title: Pause, Resume, or Abort Live Session
intent: Humans pause execution to reflect, adjust context, resume after changes, or abort dangerous runs
acceptance: Pause button on live view. Paused state persists across clients. Resume restarts from last checkpoint. Abort records reason and partial artifacts.
anti_patterns: Abort loses partial work without audit
critique_focus: Does pause preserve agent state? Does resume restart from checkpoint?
manual_simulation: Start run, click Pause in Web, verify CLI watch shows paused, resume from CLI, verify Web updates
incentive: Humans need to stop, inspect, adjust context, and resume without losing work.

title: Branch Alternative Path From Live Session
intent: Humans pause session and fork independent variant to explore different approach without losing original
acceptance: Pause button includes 'Fork' option. Fork creates new run_attempt linked to source run. Original and fork both visible in run feed.
anti_patterns: Fork not linked to parent run
critique_focus: Can humans branch experiments without losing context of original?
manual_simulation: Pause run, click Fork, verify new run appears in feed with parent link, continue both paths
incentive: Agents take paths; humans explore alternatives in parallel.

title: Edit Prompt and Re-Run Session
intent: Humans pause run, edit PROMPT.md on the fly, and restart executor from edited prompt without creating new run
acceptance: Pause session. Edit modal shows PROMPT.md. Save and re-run button. New execution linked to same run_attempt with edit trace.
critique_focus: Can humans see what they changed in the prompt before restart?
manual_simulation: Pause run, open Edit Prompt, change a step, re-run, verify edit is in transcript
incentive: Agents go wrong; humans iterate quickly without restart penalty.

title: Show File Diffs As Agents Edit
intent: Humans see unified diffs for file changes as agents make them, with approval gate before unsafe writes
acceptance: Live session shows modified files in diff view. Diff includes: old/new side-by-side or unified, syntax highlighting, line numbers. Deletions marked. File scope validation visible.
anti_patterns: Diffs shown only after session completes
critique_focus: Do humans see diffs in real-time or only after completion?
manual_simulation: Run session that edits files, view live session, click file changes, view diff
incentive: Humans need to catch bad edits before commit.

title: Configure Tool Execution Authority
intent: Projects set trust mode: review each tool, auto-allow safe actions, or danger mode for admin/destructive work
acceptance: Project settings show three radio buttons: review_each_tool (default, blocks on approval queue), auto (whitelist mode, safe tools allowed), danger (full trust, operator responsibility). Trace shows which mode governed each tool call.
anti_patterns: No visibility into permission mode used
Danger mode enables without explicit confirmation
critique_focus: Does trace explain why tool was allowed/denied?
manual_simulation: Set project to review_each_tool, start run with tool, verify approval modal appears. Change to auto, retry, verify auto-approval.
incentive: Agents touch files; trust mode must be explicit and auditable.

title: Show Which Agent is Running
intent: Humans see which agent profile/model is executing, with cost and capability visibility
acceptance: Run detail header shows: agent name, model, provider, context window/token budget, cost per run. Switchable in run replay.
critique_focus: Can humans identify which model ran each step?
manual_simulation: View run detail, see agent name and model in header, click to view capabilities
incentive: Humans need to know cost and capability of each run.

title: Graceful Empty State When No Runs Active
intent: First-time or idle users see helpful messaging: 'No active sessions', with CTA to start a run from a task
acceptance: Sessions view (or live pane in ACP) shows: icon + title + 1–2 sentence explanation + button: 'Start a Run'. Button links to task list.
anti_patterns: No CTA to start a run
Error state misread as empty state
critique_focus: Does empty state guide users to start a run?
manual_simulation: Open ACP with no active runs, verify empty state messaging and CTA
incentive: First impression matters; empty state should be helpful, not confusing.

title: Select Model Before Dispatch
intent: Humans choose executor model, validator model, planning model per task with full provider list visible
acceptance: ACP dispatch modal shows three tabs: Executor, Validator, Planner. Each lists available providers and models. Selection shows token estimate impact. Defaults cascade: task → project → global.
anti_patterns: Model picker in settings drawer instead of inline dispatch
critique_focus: Can humans pick executor and validator model independently? Do estimates update?
manual_simulation: Open dispatch modal, view model tabs, change executor model, verify context token count updates
incentive: Humans need per-task model flexibility; hiding in settings breaks discovery.

title: Show Tool Call Execution Details
intent: Humans see structured tool call timeline: what was called, with what args, success/failure, result, and copy-able output
acceptance: Timeline shows: tool name (bold), args (syntax-highlighted), result (collapsible), status badge (success/error). Copy button on result. Links to approval/permission decision if gated.
anti_patterns: Missing trace ID on tool error
critique_focus: Can humans copy tool output? Do errors show root cause?
manual_simulation: Run session, view tool calls in live view, click tool to expand args and result, copy output
incentive: Tool output is agent-human comms; must be readable and extractable.

title: Orchestrate Multi-Agent Task Execution
intent: Humans see dependency DAG of concurrent agents, assign agents to tasks, track parallel progress, and intervene on blockers
acceptance: Board view shows tasks as cards in dependency graph. Agents assigned per task. Live status: idle/running/blocked/done. Drag to reassign. Hover shows blockers.
critique_focus: Can humans visualize all dependencies and unblock stalled tasks?
manual_simulation: Create task with dependencies, assign agents, start board view, watch parallel execution
incentive: Multi-agent workflows need visible dependency management.

title: View Runs in Real-Time Feed
intent: Humans browse all active and completed runs per task/project with event history, filtered by status/agent/date
acceptance: Run feed shows: run ID, task, status, agent, elapsed time, last event timestamp. Click to expand event timeline. Filter by: status, agent, date range, project. Pagination or scroll-load.
critique_focus: Can humans find a specific run by date/status/agent?
manual_simulation: Run multiple tasks, open run feed, filter by status, view event timelines
incentive: Humans need to audit run history and troubleshoot failures.

title: Reassign Agent Mid-Execution
intent: Humans reassign a stalled or underperforming run to a different agent without losing progress
acceptance: Pause button on live run includes 'Reassign Agent' option. Modal shows available agents. Reassign releases checkout, spawns new session with same context, existing transcript is seed.
anti_patterns: Cannot reassign without canceling and restarting
critique_focus: Does new agent see prior progress and decisions?
manual_simulation: Pause run mid-execution, reassign to different agent, verify prior transcript is visible
incentive: Agents get stuck; humans need to swap agents without restart penalty.

title: Preview Run Execution Plan Before Launch
intent: Humans see what agent will do: generated PROMPT.md, file scope, approval gates, tool whitelist, model selection, before confirming dispatch
acceptance: ACP dispatch modal includes 'Preview' tab. Shows: generated PROMPT.md, declared file scope, tools that will be available, approval gates, model cost estimate. Confirm or edit before run.
anti_patterns: Cannot edit before run without cancel-restart cycle
critique_focus: Can humans review and edit the plan before the agent starts?
manual_simulation: Open dispatch modal, click Preview, review PROMPT.md and tool whitelist, edit if needed, confirm dispatch
incentive: Humans must validate plan before agent acts.

title: View Run-Generated Artifacts
intent: Humans see all artifacts created by run: diffs, specs, reports, docs, images, with source linkage and lifecycle actions
acceptance: Run detail has Artifacts pane. Shows: artifact kind (diff/doc/report), file/name, MIME, size, preview, retention policy, actions (download, archive, link to doc, promote to memory). Each artifact links back to source task/project.
anti_patterns: Artifacts not visible in run detail
critique_focus: Can humans download, archive, and promote artifacts?
manual_simulation: Complete a run, view run detail, open Artifacts pane, download a diff, link to doc
incentive: Artifacts are run output; must be discoverable and reusable.

title: Cancel Active Run
intent: Humans stop a run immediately, record reason, and preserve partial artifacts/transcript for later review
acceptance: Live run detail has Cancel button. Click opens reason modal. Confirm cancels session, records reason, saves partial artifacts with 'cancelled' marker in run status. Transcript remains visible.
anti_patterns: No way to resume after cancel
critique_focus: Are partial artifacts and transcript preserved after cancellation?
manual_simulation: Start run, click Cancel, provide reason, verify run status shows cancelled with artifacts
incentive: Agents hang or go wrong; humans need clean exit with audit trail.

title: Retry Failed Run with Visible Prompt Changes
intent: Humans retry a failed run with option to edit prompt, see diff of changes vs original, and launch new attempt
acceptance: Failed run detail shows Retry button. Click opens prompt diff editor: original on left, new on right, changes highlighted. Confirm creates new run_attempt with edit trace. Both runs in feed.
critique_focus: Can humans see exactly what they changed before retrying?
manual_simulation: Fail a run, click Retry, edit prompt in diff editor, confirm, verify both runs in feed
incentive: Agents fail; humans iterate quickly with edit trail.

title: Human Approval for Risky Actions
intent: Agents request approval before file deletions, schema changes, external API calls, or admin operations. Humans approve, deny, or request changes.
acceptance: Live run shows Approval Queue pane. Each approval shows: tool name, risk level, arguments, context. Actions: Approve, Deny, Request Info. Timeout policy configurable per project. Audit logs all decisions.
anti_patterns: No approval queue; dangerous tools auto-allowed
critique_focus: Does the approval modal show enough context to make an informed decision?
manual_simulation: Run that needs approval, view live run, see approval in queue, provide approval or denial
incentive: Agents can delete files; humans must gate destructive actions.

title: Track Run Costs and Token Usage
intent: Humans see token counts, model cost, rate-limit events, and budget consumed per run for cost visibility and optimization
acceptance: Run detail shows: total tokens (input/output), model cost estimate, rate-limit events with backoff times, token budget remaining for project/agent. Trend chart for cost over time.
critique_focus: Can humans see cost per run and adjust model selection based on cost?
manual_simulation: Complete a run, view run detail, check cost summary and token breakdown
incentive: Running agents costs money; humans need visibility to control spending.

title: Handle API Rate Limits Gracefully
intent: Agents detect rate-limit responses, record events, apply backoff, and retry transparently. Humans see backoff times and can manually retry.
acceptance: Run transcript shows rate-limit events with: status code, retry-after header, backoff calculation. Agent auto-retries with exponential backoff. Humans can force-retry. Audit records each retry.
anti_patterns: No backoff; retry immediately and get rate-limited again
critique_focus: Do rate-limit events show retry attempts and backoff times?
manual_simulation: Trigger rate limit, watch transcript for rate-limit event and retry attempts
incentive: Agents should be resilient to transient API limits.

title: Smart Retry on Classified Errors
intent: Agents classify errors (transient vs terminal), apply retry policy, and escalate to human after exhaustion. Projects configure retry budgets.
acceptance: Run transcript shows error classification: transient (network, timeout, rate-limit), terminal (invalid input, auth, deleted resource), or unknown. Agent retries transient up to budget. Humans see retry count and budget remaining.
anti_patterns: Terminal errors not distinguished from transient
No budget enforcement; retry loop hangs
critique_focus: Are errors classified correctly? Does agent stop retrying after budget exhaustion?
manual_simulation: Introduce error, watch error classification and retry behavior in transcript
incentive: Agents should retry transient errors but fail fast on terminal errors.

title: Propagate Trace IDs Through Event Stream
intent: Every event (tool call, approval, file edit, error) carries trace ID for end-to-end correlability across Web/CLI/TUI/API
acceptance: Every event row in transcript shows: event ID (bold), trace ID (smaller, monospace), timestamp. CLI JSON output includes event_id and trace_id on every line. Error messages include trace ID.
anti_patterns: No way to correlate events across clients
Trace ID visible in logs but not in UI
critique_focus: Can humans click an event and find all related events via trace ID?
manual_simulation: Run a session with error, view event, copy trace ID, search logs for that ID
incentive: Trace IDs are the bedrock of observability; must be always visible.

title: Run Feed on Mobile Devices
intent: Humans monitor and control runs on phones: compact status cards, swipe/tap actions, minimal scrolling, clear status colors
acceptance: Mobile view shows run status cards in list (one per run). Card shows: task name, status badge, elapsed time, agent, last event. Tap to open detail. Swipe for quick actions (pause, cancel). No horizontal scroll.
anti_patterns: Run feed unreadable on mobile (too wide, text too small)
Actions buried in modal instead of swipe
Status colors not high contrast on mobile
critique_focus: Can humans pause/cancel a run with one tap?
manual_simulation: Open mobile view (or test responsive at 375px width), view run feed, tap status card, use swipe actions
incentive: Humans run agents from phones; mobile UX must be frictionless.

title: Display Streamed Model Output in Real-Time
intent: Humans see agent messages appear word-by-word as they are streamed, with no UI lag or buffering jumps
acceptance: Transcript shows: agent message appearing in real-time, streaming indicator (cursor or spinner) during stream, final message stable after stream ends. No jumps or rewrites. Copy button works on both partial and final text.
anti_patterns: Message appears all at once (no streaming perception)
critique_focus: Does streaming feel smooth or do messages jump around?
manual_simulation: Run with streaming output, watch transcript for smooth appearance of text
incentive: Streaming gives perception of responsiveness; jumpy rendering breaks confidence.

title: Email and password login with optional magic link
intent: Support both traditional email+password login and passwordless magic link option
acceptance: User can log in with email and password
Magic link option is discoverable
Login errors distinguish between invalid email and invalid password without leaking user existence
Session created and stored in secure HTTP-only cookie
Throttle limits apply per email address
anti_patterns: Password reset link in login error leaks whether email exists
Login form shows placeholder text that suggests passwords are stored plaintext
Successful login redirect is hardcoded instead of respecting origin parameter
manual_simulation: Login with magic link if enabled
incentive: core identity

title: User signup with email verification and workspace setup
intent: Allow new users to create account and immediately set up a workspace
acceptance: Signup form requires email and password
Password strength indicator present
Email verification sent immediately after signup
Workspace slug validated against disallowed list
First admin user created during setup, subsequent users invite-only
Setup guard prevents signup if workspace already initialized
anti_patterns: Signup form requires unnecessary fields that users must figure out
Workspace slug auto-generated without user input or easily changed
Verification email sent but signup flow doesn't explain verification requirement
Workspace creation fails silently without explaining why slug is rejected
manual_simulation: Setup workspace with disallowed slug (should fail)
Verify first admin user created and can log in
Attempt signup again (should redirect to login)
incentive: user onboarding

title: Password reset via email link with token expiry
intent: Allow users to reset forgotten password through email token flow
acceptance: Forgot password form accepts email only
Email sent with reset link containing opaque token
Token expires after 1 hour or first use
Reset link directs to form pre-filled with email
Password reset form shows strength indicator
After reset, old sessions revoked and user redirected to login
anti_patterns: Password reset email sent to email that's not in system (leaks user existence)
Token visible in browser URL without encryption (token in hash is OK, in path is not)
Reset form doesn't show which email it's for (user confusion with multiple accounts)
Reset successful but user not told to check email if MFA or wait time applies
manual_simulation: Request password reset with valid email
Request with multiple emails concurrently (only one should work)
Attempt to reuse same token (should fail)
incentive: account recovery

title: Two-factor authentication setup with TOTP (authenticator app)
intent: Allow users to add TOTP-based 2FA for additional account security
acceptance: 2FA setup initiated from account settings
QR code displayed for scanning with authenticator app
User enters 6-digit code from authenticator to confirm setup
Recovery codes generated and presented for backup
Recovery codes can be regenerated and old ones invalidated
2FA enabled status displayed in profile
anti_patterns: QR code generated but secret key not shown (user cannot backup manually)
Recovery codes only shown once without copy/save option
2FA setup doesn't require current password confirmation (account takeover risk)
Recovery codes not marked as single-use or limited (reuse attacks)
manual_simulation: Scan QR code with authenticator app
Enter code from authenticator to confirm
Save recovery codes to secure location
Disable 2FA and re-enable to test recovery
Attempt login with 2FA enabled and expired code (should ask for refresh)
incentive: security

title: 2FA verification during login and recovery code fallback
intent: Require 2FA code entry after successful password authentication if 2FA enabled
acceptance: After password verified, user prompted for 2FA code
Code entry form accepts 6-digit or recovery code
Code expires after 60 seconds if user closes form and reopens
Too many failed attempts (5+) lock account for 15 minutes
Successful 2FA creates session and stores device fingerprint if remembered
Remember device option shown but not enabled by default
anti_patterns: Login form shows whether user has 2FA enabled before authentication (leaks info)
2FA code field prefills or shows digits as user types (keylogger risk)
Remember device enabled by default on shared computer scenario
Failed 2FA attempts not logged for audit/anti-fraud
manual_simulation: Enter invalid 2FA code multiple times to trigger lockout
Use recovery code instead of 2FA code
Select remember device and verify remembered on next login
Test code expiry by waiting >60s and closing form
incentive: security

title: Single sign-on via Google OAuth2 with automatic user creation
intent: Allow users to sign in using existing Google account without managing password
acceptance: SSO provider shown on login page if enabled in workspace
User redirected to Google OAuth consent screen
After consent, user email extracted and account created or linked if exists
Automatic workspace assignment based on email domain or default role
MFA requirement checked after SSO (if workspace enforces MFA, SSO users exempt if TOTP cannot apply)
SSO enforcement flag prevents password login for affected users
anti_patterns: SSO callback stores auth code in URL history or localStorage without rotation
Email verified flag not set for SSO accounts (they should be implicit verified)
SSO enforcement breaks existing password accounts without migration path
Multiple SSO providers account mapping ambiguous (which account is primary)
manual_simulation: Attempt Google login on workspace with SSO disabled (should not appear)
Attempt Google login on workspace with SSO enabled and allowed domain
Consent and verify account created with verified email
Attempt Google login with email outside allowed domain (should fail)
Enable SSO enforcement and verify password login disabled
Test callback error handling and redirect to error page
incentive: frictionless auth

title: Single sign-on via GitHub and OIDC providers
intent: Support GitHub OAuth2 and generic OpenID Connect providers for flexibility
acceptance: GitHub OAuth2 provider available as built-in option
Generic OIDC provider configurable with discovery URL and client credentials
User granted consent for email scope at minimum
Returned claims mapped to user email and name fields
Account created or linked based on email match
Existing password account linked if email matches and user consents
anti_patterns: OIDC configuration stored in plaintext settings (should be encrypted)
No client secret validation in callback (CSRF/token swap risk)
User identity claims cached without expiry (stale email sync)
OIDC provider credential rotation breaks login without admin awareness
manual_simulation: Enable generic OIDC provider with a test identity provider
Attempt OIDC login and verify claims mapped correctly
Test account linking with existing password account
Test revocation/uninstall of OAuth provider (should fail logins)
incentive: enterprise flexibility

title: Account lockout after repeated failed login attempts
intent: Protect against brute force attacks by temporarily locking account
acceptance: Account locked after 5 failed login attempts in 15 minutes
Lockout duration is 15 minutes and automatically expires
Lockout applies to email+password attempts only, not SSO
User notified of lockout status and when account will unlock
Lockout event logged to audit trail with IP and user agent
Admin can manually unlock account before lockout expires
anti_patterns: Lockout message doesn't say when user can retry (user frustration)
Lockout triggered per IP instead of per user (shared IP scenarios fail)
Lockout persists forever after reaching max (user locked out permanently)
No audit of lockout events (no forensics if account was attacked)
manual_simulation: Login with wrong password 5 times in 15 minutes
Verify account locked and receive notification
Wait 15 minutes and attempt login again
Verify login succeeds after lockout expires
Admin manually unlock account while locked
Check audit log shows lockout and unlock events
incentive: security

title: Email address verification with token and resend flow
intent: Verify user email is legitimate and owned by user during signup/email change
acceptance: Verification email sent immediately after signup with link containing token
Link directs to auto-verify page that confirms email
Verification token expires after 24 hours
Unverified email shown in user profile as unverified
Resend button available if token expired or lost
Resend throttled to once per 60 seconds
anti_patterns: Verification token sent in plaintext email (should be encrypted or random enough)
Verified flag checked in every request (perf issue)
User can perform sensitive actions with unverified email
Resend button not visible or requires finding lost email link
manual_simulation: Signup and check verification email received
Click verification link and confirm auto-verify
Attempt to resend more than once per 60s (should throttle)
Attempt action requiring verified email with unverified address
incentive: security compliance

title: Create and manage API tokens for programmatic access
intent: Allow users to create scoped tokens for API access without sharing password
acceptance: API token creation in account settings requires current password confirmation
Token name and scopes specified at creation (read, write, admin)
Token displayed once at creation and must be copied (not retrievable later)
Token includes workspace and user context for audit
Token expiry configurable (30, 90, 365 days or never)
Token revocation immediate and audited
anti_patterns: API token shown in plain text without copy button (user frustration)
Token creation doesn't require password confirmation (compromised account can create token)
Token scopes not enforced in API (token bypass risk)
Revoked tokens cached and still work for grace period (stale revocation)
manual_simulation: Create API token with read scope
Use token for API request and verify it works
Revoke token and verify API request fails
Check token audit log shows creation and revocation with timestamps
incentive: API access

title: Workspace creation with slug validation and default settings
intent: Allow users to create new workspaces with unique slug and customizable defaults
acceptance: Workspace creation form shows name and slug fields
Slug validated as unique and not in disallowed list
Slug auto-normalized to lowercase alphanumeric+hyphen
Default member role selectable (member, guest, or restricted)
Default space created with same name as workspace
Logo/avatar upload available at creation or later in settings
Workspace member count initialized to 1 (creator)
anti_patterns: Slug validation happens on save instead of real-time (poor UX feedback)
Auto-generated slug doesn't match user input (user confusion)
Workspace created but default space fails silently (broken invariant)
Default member role not shown in settings (user doesn't know workspace defaults)
manual_simulation: Create workspace with disallowed slug (should show error)
Create workspace with slug containing spaces or capitals (should normalize)
Verify default space created with correct name
Change default member role in workspace settings
Verify only creator is member until invites accepted
incentive: core product

title: Workspace switcher in top navigation with quick actions
intent: Allow fast switching between workspaces and creating new workspace
acceptance: Top bar shows current workspace name and avatar
Clicking opens dropdown with list of user's workspaces
Each workspace entry shows name, logo, and member count
Leave workspace action available if not last admin
Create new workspace action at bottom of list
Recently used workspace sorting or sticky current workspace
Mobile displays workspace name only, click to expand menu
anti_patterns: Workspace list doesn't show which is current (user confusion)
Switching workspace doesn't preserve browser history (back button broken)
Creating new workspace hides form in dropdown instead of modal (small screens fail)
Leave workspace doesn't warn if user is last admin (irreversible)
manual_simulation: Open workspace switcher and verify all workspaces listed
Switch to another workspace and verify page refreshes
Attempt to leave workspace as member (should succeed)
Attempt to leave workspace as last admin (should warn)
incentive: core UX

title: Invite new members by email with role assignment
intent: Allow admins to invite users by email and assign roles before they join
acceptance: Invite form accepts email address and role selection
Email must pass whitelist/domain validation if configured
Existing users get added directly, new users get invitation email
Invitation email includes join link with token
Invite link works without login, prompts for password if new user
Role can be changed before user accepts invitation
Invitation list shows email, role, inviter, and invited date
Expired or invalid invitations cleaned up automatically after 30 days
anti_patterns: Invite sent but user not notified that they were invited (user confusion)
Join link sends to generic login instead of auto-filling email (wrong account)
Role change after invite not reflected in acceptance (inconsistency)
Invitation list shows all invites without pagination (perf issue for large workspaces)
Revoke invitation doesn't verify admin permission (privilege escalation)
manual_simulation: Invite new user and check email received
Click invite link and create account
Check invited user has correct role assigned
List pending invitations and verify correct info shown
Try to use invite link after 30 days (should fail)
incentive: onboarding

title: Share workspace join link for guest invitations
intent: Allow creating reusable workspace join links without specifying email addresses
acceptance: Generate workspace join link from members settings
Link is time-limited (7 days) and revocable
Link includes role specification at creation time
Unlimited uses per link until revoked or expired
Join link shows workspace info before sign-up
New users signing up via link auto-added to workspace with assigned role
Link can be regenerated with new role assignment
anti_patterns: Link doesn't show workspace name before signup (user doesn't know what they're joining)
Joining via link doesn't verify email (spambots can join)
No way to track which users joined via which link (audit gap)
manual_simulation: Generate workspace join link with guest role
Share link and test joining as new user
Verify new user has guest role assigned
Change link role and test both old and new links
Attempt to use expired link (should fail)
Revoke link and verify no further joins possible
incentive: frictionless onboarding

title: Member list with search and filter by role
intent: Allow workspace admins to find and manage members efficiently
acceptance: Members list shows email, name, role, status (active/inactive), join date
Search filters by email or name (case-insensitive substring match)
Filter by role shows owner/admin/member/guest members
Inactive members (last active >90 days) marked with indicator
Pagination or virtual scroll for >100 members
Column sorting by name, role, or join date
Member status (online/offline) if available
Export members list as CSV with selected columns
anti_patterns: Search is slow or blocks UI (no debounce)
Filter by role doesn't show count of each role (user guessing)
Inactive user indicator doesn't explain what inactive means
Export doesn't include important columns like email or role
No way to bulk action members (change role, remove, export subset)
manual_simulation: Search for member by partial email
Filter by member role and verify list updates
Identify and verify inactive member status
Export members list and verify CSV content
Test pagination or virtual scroll with >100 members
Attempt bulk role change for multiple members
incentive: workspace management

title: Change member role with approval and audit trail
intent: Allow workspace admins to update member permissions without removing and re-inviting
acceptance: Role change available from members list dropdown or member detail
Current role shown and new role required
Change requires admin confirmation with reason (optional)
Role change logged to audit trail with actor, timestamp, before/after
User notified of role change in activity feed or email
Owner cannot be changed (only account owner can change owner)
Effective permission scope updated in real-time
anti_patterns: Role change silent with no confirmation (accidental changes)
Role change doesn't show what permissions will change (user confusion)
Downgrading last admin role not prevented (workspace lock-out)
Role change audit entry doesn't show who made change (non-repudiation issue)
Old role cached in UI until page refresh (inconsistency)
manual_simulation: Change member role from member to admin
Check audit log shows role change with details
Verify member receives notification of new role
Attempt to change last admin role (should prevent)
Verify new permissions take effect immediately for member
Change role again and confirm can revert
incentive: access control

title: Remove member from workspace with data retention options
intent: Allow admins to remove members and define what happens to their content
acceptance: Remove member action available from members list dropdown
Confirmation dialog shows member email and workspace name
Removal options: revoke access immediately or set deactivation date
Deactivated member access retained for audit but content ownership unchanged
Member data (docs, pages) can be reassigned to another member or marked archived
Access revocation takes effect immediately for realtime sessions
Audit log records removal with actor, reason, and data disposition
anti_patterns: Remove member doesn't show what data they own (surprise after removal)
Immediate removal deletes member data without option to preserve (data loss)
Deactivation doesn't actually revoke access (false confidence)
No way to re-enable removed member except re-invite (friction)
Audit doesn't show what content was affected by member removal
manual_simulation: Remove member immediately and verify access revoked in real-time
Attempt to access workspace as removed member (should fail)
Remove member with deactivation date and verify access still works until date
Mark member data as archived instead of reassigning
Check audit log shows member removal with data disposition
Attempt to re-add removed member and verify fresh invite
incentive: access control

title: Display role definitions and permission matrix for reference
intent: Help users understand what each role can do
acceptance: Role definitions page shows Owner, Admin, Member, Guest roles
Each role lists capabilities: create space, manage members, edit settings, delete, etc.
Permission inheritance shown (Owner inherits all Member permissions)
Capability descriptions are action-oriented and specific
Space-level and workspace-level permissions separated
Permission matrix downloadable or printable as reference

intent: False-green doctor is dangerous; users rely on green indicator to trust system health; degraded conditions must be visible at a glance.
acceptance: Doctor summary: shows ✓ all healthy OR ⚠ X issues / degraded OR ✗ broken
Subsystem list: always shows all items, degraded items in yellow, broken in red
If any subsystem degraded: doctor header shows ⚠ warning color
Summary message: e.g. '⚠ MCP server openclaw offline, rate limit 85%'
anti_patterns: Doctor green with MCP server offline
No degraded status indicator in header
Summary shows only healthy systems, omits warnings
manual_simulation: Healthy system: doctor shows ✓ all healthy in green header
Disconnect MCP server: doctor shows ⚠ degraded in yellow
Verify doctor never shows green if any subsystem warning/broken
incentive: Safety: false-green doctor erodes trust and masks real issues; must show degraded clearly

title: Inference backend status panel showing health, degraded conditions, and fallback model availability
intent: Users must know if inference is impaired: slow (degraded) vs unavailable (broken), and what fallback models are available.
acceptance: Status panel shows: provider (claude/openai/mistral), model, status (healthy/degraded/offline)
Degraded indicators: rate limit warnings, slow response time (>5s), quota exhaustion
Reason: captures error message or slow condition
Fallback model: shows alternate model configured (or none)
Last check and response time (ms)
Action: switch provider, adjust rate limit, view quota usage
anti_patterns: Status green but inference timing out
Degraded conditions not visually distinguished from healthy
Fallback model not shown when primary is degraded
manual_simulation: View inference status, check healthy model
Trigger rate limit (fake), verify degraded status
incentive: Reliability: degraded status visibility prevents silent slowdowns and quota shock

title: Inference model list with pull/sync, version, context window, and cost-per-1k-token display
intent: Users must see available models, their capabilities, and pull new models locally without CLI commands.
acceptance: Model table: name, version, provider, status (available/downloaded/pulling), context window, cost, last updated
Filter: by provider, downloaded only, capability (vision/function-call)
Sort: by popularity, context size, cost
Pull button: downloads model locally (spinner, progress bar)
Sync/refresh button: checks for new versions
Disk usage per model, total storage used
CLI: `fusion models list`, `fusion models pull <model>`
anti_patterns: Model list without cost or context window
No visual distinction between available and downloaded
Sync without checking for version updates
Mobile list without collapse for long text
manual_simulation: Click pull on available model, check progress bar
Complete pull, verify status changes to downloaded
incentive: Convenience: model pull UI without CLI reduces onboarding friction

title: Inference provider config panel with credentials input and test API call button
intent: Users must configure providers (API keys, endpoints) and verify connectivity without manual curl commands.
acceptance: Config panel per provider: name, API key input (masked), base URL (optional), timeout (ms)
Credentials: stored in ~/.fusion/credentials.json (encrypted or OS keychain)
Test button: calls provider API with dummy request, shows result (latency, version, error)
Result: ✓ connected, quota remaining / ✗ failed (reason)
Save button: validates credentials before persist
CLI: `fusion config provider claude --api-key=...`, `fusion provider test claude`
anti_patterns: API key input shown in plaintext
Test without error handling or timeout
Test result without latency or quota info
manual_simulation: Click test, verify ✓ and latency shown
Try invalid key, verify ✗ and error message
Save and verify stored in credentials.json
incentive: Onboarding: provider config UI eliminates trial-and-error API key debugging

title: Credential list with rotate, archive, and source integration indicator
intent: Users must manage API keys, tokens, and secrets securely without viewing plaintext; rotation and archiving track credential lifecycle.
acceptance: Credential table: source (claude/github/openrouter), name, type (API key/token), status (active/archived), created date, last rotated, days until expiry (if set)
Actions: rotate (generates new, archives old), archive (marks inactive), delete (permanent, warns dependent configs)
Rotation result: new value masked, old value archived, last rotated timestamp updated
List shows active and archived tabs
Dependent configs: show which providers/skills use credential
anti_patterns: List mixing active and archived without separation
interactions: confirm rotation, view new masked value
manual_simulation: Load credential list, verify active tab
Click rotate on Claude API key
Verify old key archived, new key generated
Switch to archived tab, verify old key listed
Attempt delete active key, verify warning
incentive: Security: credential rotation and archiving enforce key hygiene without manual file editing

title: Anti-pattern: Credential values must never be visible in plaintext in UI, storage, or logs
intent: Prevent accidental credential exposure in screenshots, debugging, or data breaches; all credentials must be masked or encrypted at rest and in transit.
acceptance: UI: API keys shown as masked (e.g., *****key123 last 4 chars only)
Storage: ~/.fusion/credentials.json encrypted with OS keychain or AES
Logs: credential values never logged, use placeholder (e.g., <REDACTED>)
Paste action: credential value input only visible while typing, masked after blur
Screenshots: masked values preserved in any exported/shared images
anti_patterns: Full API key visible in credentials list
Credentials logged in error logs or stdout
Credentials in plaintext in config files
Credentials not masked in clipboard or undo history
interactions: paste API key into input field
trigger error, check logs for redaction
export settings, verify credentials excluded or masked
manual_simulation: Paste API key in provider config
Verify shows only last 4 chars after blur
Trigger error, view logs and verify <REDACTED>
Export settings JSON, verify credentials excluded
Take screenshot, verify API key masked
incentive: Security: plaintext credential exposure is critical vulnerability; masking is mandatory

title: Connector list with enable/disable toggle and configuration panel per source
intent: Users must manage integrations (GitHub, Linear, Slack, etc.) without manual config file editing; enable/disable must be fast and reversible.
acceptance: Connector table: name (github/linear/slack), status (enabled/disabled), auth status (not connected/connected/expired)
Enable toggle: immediately activates connector
Configure button: opens panel with credential input, permissions preview, last sync timestamp
Scope indicators: what data will sync (commits, PRs, issues, etc.)
Auth status: ✓ connected since [date] / ⚠ token expired / ✗ not configured
Last sync: shows sync timestamp, trigger manual sync button
anti_patterns: Expired token not shown as warning
No way to manually trigger sync
manual_simulation: Toggle GitHub on, verify enabled immediately
incentive: Integration UX: fast enable/disable and clear scope reduce configuration friction

title: Cost and usage breakdown by provider, model, and date range with quota warnings
intent: Users must understand inference spend and quota usage; cost transparency prevents surprise bills and guides model selection.
acceptance: Breakdown by: provider (claude/openai/mistral), model, date range (7d/30d/ytd), cost in USD
Chart: line or bar showing daily spend trend
Table: model, token count (input+output), cost per 1k, total cost
Quota indicators: remaining budget per provider, % used, warning if >80%
Export: CSV with detailed cost breakdown
Forecast: projected spend if current rate continues
anti_patterns: Cost view without date range selector
Export without timestamp and model detail
manual_simulation: Load cost panel, view last 30 days
incentive: Cost control: transparent usage and quota warnings prevent bill shock and guide optimization

title: Quota and rate-limit visibility panel with current usage, resets, and throttle policy
intent: Users must know current quota usage and rate-limit window to avoid cascading request failures and understand throttle behavior.
acceptance: Quota panel per provider: requests/min limit, remaining this minute, reset in X seconds
Requests/day limit, usage today, reset in X hours
Token quota if provider enforces it (e.g., Claude has request quota)
Throttle policy: backoff strategy (exponential, linear, immediate retry)
Warning indicators: 80% usage shows ⚠, 100% shows ✗
Reset countdown: live update as window expires
anti_patterns: Rate limit not distinguished from quota
incentive: Reliability: quota visibility prevents silent cascading failures and guides request pacing

title: Mobile observability views: condensed error log, doctor status, quota meter, and settings
intent: Mobile users must access core observability features with touch-friendly layouts and responsive data density.
acceptance: Mobile doctor: card layout with subsystem status (✓/⚠/✗) and last check time
Mobile error log: expandable list, severity color coding, tap for detail panel
Mobile quota: single metric per provider (% used) with color (green/yellow/red)
Settings: accordion sections (telemetry, providers, connectors), toggle switches
Breakpoint: optimized for 375px+ width (iPhone SE and up)
Touch-friendly: buttons 48px min, no hover-dependent interactions
anti_patterns: Table layout used on mobile (horizontal scroll)
interactions: tap quota card to view provider details
manual_simulation: View doctor cards, verify all subsystems visible
Tap subsystem, verify detail panel opens
View error log, tap error, verify detail expands
Check settings, toggle telemetry, verify persists
incentive: Mobile parity: observability on mobile enables diagnostics from any device

title: Anti-pattern: Every observability surface must expose and link trace IDs across error, audit, run, and event data
intent: Trace IDs are the universal correlation key; absence of trace IDs in observability surfaces breaks root cause analysis.
acceptance: Error log: trace ID column visible, clickable to filter by trace
Audit log: causation_id or source_trace_id column, clickable
Run detail: trace ID in header, visible in events and spans
Event timeline: each event shows trace ID and parent trace ID if nested
Doctor probe result: includes probe_trace_id
CLI JSON output: includes trace_id or causation_id field
anti_patterns: Error log without trace ID column
Run events not tagged with trace ID
Filtering by trace ID not available
CLI JSON output missing trace IDs
Trace IDs not correlated across surfaces (web vs CLI)
interactions: navigate trace from error to run to task
CLI: fetch JSON with trace IDs
manual_simulation: Error log: find trace ID column, click to filter
Audit log: click causation_id, verify related events filter
Run detail: check trace ID in header and events
Doctor probe: verify result includes probe_trace_id
CLI: `fusion errors list --json` includes trace_id field
incentive: Observability: trace ID correlation is foundational for root cause analysis and debugging

title: Task list page with kanban, list, table, calendar layouts
intent: User views all tasks in project grouped by state, assignee, priority, date. Switches layouts via buttons. Filters persist per view.
acceptance: Board shows cards grouped by state with drag/drop reorder
List view shows compact rows with inline edit
Table view columns toggle and persist
Calendar view shows due dates as events

No trace ID in network errors
Keyboard shortcut not working in search field

interactions.expected: Board view renders

critique_focus: Does drag/drop work on mobile touch?
Are all 4 layout types fully featured?
manual_simulation: Filter by assignee=me, verify only matching tasks appear

acceptance: Title and description editable inline
All properties show and allow quick edit
Comments thread shows below description
Activity log shows state changes

No indication when field is loading

Click state dropdown, select new state

title: Task creation modal with all required fields and validation

Create button disabled until title filled

No error message for field validation

critique_focus: Are all required fields highlighted before submit?
manual_simulation: Click create, leave title blank, try submit
Fill title and create, verify task appears

title: Task status lifecycle: backlog, unstarted, started, completed states with state groups
intent: Tasks move through defined state groups. Each project can customize state names. UI shows state groups as columns.
acceptance: Default state groups: Backlog, Unstarted, Started, Completed
Board shows state groups as columns
Moving task updates state

interactions.expected: Card moves, state updates

critique_focus: Can project lead create new state groups?
manual_simulation: Drag task from Backlog to Started

title: Subtasks and parent task relationships
intent: User can create subtasks under parent task. Subtask count shown on parent. Parent link shown on subtask.
acceptance: Parent task shows subtask count badge
Subtask row shows parent link

Delete parent offers options

title: Task dependencies: blocking and blocked-by relationships with dependency graph

acceptance: Link dialog offers blocks, is blocked by, relates to

Run button disabled if blocking dependencies unresolved

Try to link C blocks A, verify error

title: Cycles: Linear-style sprints with start/end dates and issue tracking
intent: User creates cycles with start/end dates. Moves tasks into cycle. Views progress. Archives completed cycles.

Module status tracking

Project card shows quick-actions
Project settings available

Remove member with confirmation

Bulk actions toolbar

Includes illustration/icon
Copy is friendly and actionable

Validation error shows field name

Toast notification shows 5 seconds

title: Project workbench keeps Plane-style multi-layout parity
intent: Expand Fulcrum project work so one project workbench can switch between board, list, spreadsheet, calendar, and Gantt/timeline without changing the underlying task set, filters, or saved-view identity.
acceptance: Project board URL exposes layout switcher with board, list, table, calendar, timeline choices.
Switching layouts preserves active project, selected saved view, filters, grouping, sort, and selected task ids.
All layouts call the same work-management aggregate instead of each route issuing separate CRUD queries.
Calendar and timeline are disabled only when required date/dependency data is absent and explain the missing fields.
anti_patterns: Separate unrelated routes with divergent filters for each layout.
Calendar-only task copies or timeline-only dependency copies.
Web component stitching direct database data instead of service aggregate.
interactions: Open project board, change layout to table, add a filter, switch to calendar, verify filter persists.
Select three tasks in list, switch to board, run bulk status move.
Use keyboard shortcut to cycle layouts and verify focus remains inside the workbench.
critique_focus: Does the UX feel like Plane's issue workspace while preserving Fulcrum's task/run/doc graph instead of becoming a generic kanban clone?
manual_simulation: As a project lead, review blocked tasks in board view, switch to spreadsheet for bulk triage, then calendar for due-date risk without rebuilding the query.
incentive: Turns Fulcrum work management into a durable command center instead of disconnected task views.

title: Saved views span project and workspace work scopes
intent: Add Plane-inspired saved views that persist layout, filters, display properties, grouping, sort, access, and scope for project-level and workspace-level work queues.
acceptance: SavedView stores scope as project or workspace and validates access level.
Saved view can open in board, list, table, calendar, or timeline with one shared filter model.
Workspace views can include tasks from multiple projects while still showing project badges and repo context.
Saved views have create, rename, duplicate, delete, and default-view actions.

Saved filters tied only to board route query params.
Private view visibility enforced only in the client.

Duplicate a project view, change layout from table to board, save as private.
Open saved view from command palette and verify project/repo context remains visible.

manual_simulation: As an engineering manager, save a cross-project 'agent blocked' view and revisit it after switching projects.
incentive: Saved views become the reusable lens for every planning, review, and dispatch workflow.

incentive: Experienced users work faster; no forced muscle memory changes

title: Real-time external annotations from other reviewers (SSE stream)

acceptance: Review session has unique ID; reviewer opens plan → server establishes SSE stream for annotations; when reviewer A adds comment, reviewer B sees comment appear immediately (within 1s); annotations include author + timestamp; deletion annotations do not conflict (both can mark same section); export includes all annotations from all reviewers
anti_patterns: annotation from reviewer A visible to reviewer B but not in export (lost history)

comment from reviewer A overwrites comment from reviewer B (last-write-wins)

critique_focus: SSE reconnection on network flake; message ordering on high latency; author identity verification; comment deletion handling
manual_simulation: 1. Share plan URL with colleague. 2. Both open in separate windows. 3. Add comment on Section 1. 4. Colleague sees comment appear in real-time. 5. Colleague adds comment on Section 2. 6. See colleague's comment appear. 7. Both approve → feedback shows 2 approvals from 2 users.
incentive: Async multi-reviewer collaboration; no manual reconciliation of feedback
